cases.situation: My son Eli (Year 8) got a zero on his science project for being 'late', but Google Classroom shows he submitted it Sunday night before the Monday deadline. Teacher is Mr Barnes.
cases.reply: Hi Mr Barnes, I'm Eli Carter's dad (8C). Eli's science project was marked late with a zero, but Google Classroom shows he submitted it at 7:40pm on Sunday 20 September, before the Monday deadline; screenshot attached. Could you take a look and let me know if I've missed something? Thanks for checking, Daniel Carter
cases.note: A question, not a verdict: the timestamp does the arguing, and 'if I've missed something' lets him fix it without losing face.

cases.situation: 女儿三年级，最近每天晚上写数学作业写到十点，一边写一边哭，说听不懂。班主任兼数学老师是张老师。
cases.reply: 张老师您好，我是三年级二班刘可欣的妈妈。可欣最近两周数学作业经常写到晚上十点，边写边哭，说两位数乘法课上没太听懂。想问问您在课堂上有没有观察到类似的情况？我们在家每天陪她练15分钟口算。您这周哪天方便通个电话？放学后或中午都可以。谢谢您！
cases.note: 只说看到的事实，再问老师看到了什么，不先下结论说作业太多。

cases.situation: Emailed my son's teacher Ms Rivera on Sept 14 and Sept 21 about a kid shoving him in the bus line, twice leaving a bruise. No reply either time. Want to go to the assistant principal, Mr Grant.
cases.reply:
Dear Mr Grant,
I'm writing about my son Noah Kim (4th grade, Ms Rivera's class). Since early September another student has been shoving him in the bus line after school, twice leaving a bruise on his arm. I emailed Ms Rivera on 14 and 21 September (copies below) and haven't heard back, and it's still happening. Could you let me know the school's next steps, and when we could meet this week?
Thank you,
Grace Kim
cases.note: Escalate with dates and copies, no criticism of the teacher. If Noah is being hurt again, contact the safeguarding lead the same day.

cases.situation: My daughter Nora (Grade 5, Ms. Kowalski's class) was just diagnosed with ADHD. She says she can't focus in her seat by the window and keeps getting in trouble for unfinished work. I'd like to talk to the teacher before the November conferences.
cases.reply: Hi Ms. Kowalski, I'm Nora Brennan's dad. Nora was recently diagnosed with ADHD, and she's told us she finds it hard to focus in her seat by the window and often doesn't finish classwork. I'd really like to hear what you've seen in class before we assume anything. At home we've started breaking homework into 15-minute blocks with short breaks, which seems to help. Could we meet for 20 minutes in the next couple of weeks? I'm free after 3:30 any day, or happy to do a call. Thank you.
cases.note: Share the diagnosis only as far as it helps the teacher, then ask what she sees instead of prescribing a seat change in the first message.

cases.situation: My son Kai (Year 10) got a Saturday detention for 'defiance' after refusing to take his hoodie off in class on Monday. He has an eczema flare on his arms and was embarrassed. Head of year is Mr Okafor; detention is this Saturday, Oct 3.
cases.reply: Dear Mr Okafor, I'm Kai Tanaka's mum (10B). Kai has a Saturday detention on 3 October for refusing to take off his hoodie in class on Monday. He has an eczema flare on his arms at the moment and was embarrassed to show it, which he should have explained rather than just refusing. Could the detention be reconsidered, and could he wear a plain long-sleeved top under his blazer until it clears? I can send a note from his GP, and I'm free to talk any afternoon this week. Thank you, Emi Tanaka
cases.note: Disagreeing with a sanction: give the missing fact, concede Kai's part, and ask for a decision plus a practical fix.

cases.situation: I emailed my daughter Mia's Grade 7 teacher, Mr. Hale, that she's spending 3 hours a night on homework. He replied the assignments are designed for 45 minutes and maybe she's distracted at home. I don't want a fight.
cases.reply: Thanks for getting back to me so quickly, Mr. Hale, that's useful to know, 45 minutes is a lot less than we're seeing. This week I'll keep a simple log of what Mia works on and for how long, with her phone in the kitchen, and send it to you on Friday. If it's still well over, could we meet for 15 minutes next week to see where she's getting stuck?
cases.note: Don't argue with the implied criticism; turn it into shared evidence and a small next step.

cases.situation: 儿子乐乐上四年级，10月15号、16号（周四周五）要回老家参加外婆八十大寿，得请两天假。班主任是李老师。想提前说一声，也问问落下的功课怎么补。
cases.reply: 李老师您好，我是四年级三班王乐乐的妈妈。乐乐外婆10月17日过八十大寿，我们要回老家一趟，想给他请10月15日周四和16日周五两天假，19日周一正常上学。想问一下这两天的作业和课堂内容，能不能麻烦您提前告诉我们，或者让同桌帮忙记一下？我们会在路上带着他补上。给您添麻烦了，谢谢！
cases.note: 计划中的请假要提前说，给出准确日期和返校日，再主动问怎么补课，老师更好安排。

cases.situation: My ex and I separated over the summer and our son Sam (Year 3, Mr Doyle's class) now lives with me Monday to Wednesday. All the school emails and reading-record notes go only to his mum. I want to be copied in, and give the teacher a heads-up.
cases.reply: Hi Mr Doyle, I'm Sam Reid's dad (3D). Sam's mum and I separated over the summer, and Sam is now with me Monday to Wednesday and with her the rest of the week. Could you add me to the class emails and reading-record notes, at tom.reid@fastmail.com, so both homes stay in the loop? He seems to be handling it well, and we're keeping homework and bedtimes the same at both houses. If you notice anything in class, I'd really appreciate hearing about it. Thanks, Tom Reid
cases.note: Family change: facts only, no blame on the other parent, one practical ask, and an open door for the teacher to share what she sees.
